answer: The keeper gauges the mountain lake every week and measures the outflow at the dam, entering both in the gauge book. A sable level copied from another lake fails the book: at the vine of the gauge the water must match the lake's own rain, and a copied level belongs to another valley. Forging a year of gauges means bribing the keeper, faking fifty-two entries and paying 8,900, while the tundra book in the dam office is kept for the life of the lake, so a lake whose level was never gauged is struck off.
